why: Max ruled on 2026-10-31 for a reviewed hand pin from 0.49.27 to 0.50.0. Each reason group was checked against the module and crate sources at their tags. (1) iam env: the one non-image change in the 83-object render is the added entry KEY_IDENTITY_ADOPT=observe on Deployment/iam. iam 0.18.0 (iam#134, ADR-1085, ADR-1091) makes the key required by the binary, and the chart ships observe as its default. In observe mode iam runs the adoption proof and logs it, never calls AdoptKeyIdentity and never exits, so the pod stays UNVERIFIED, as a pre-marker store such as kind-yadgar is today (iam#134). iam-db 0.15.14 serves ListKeyIdentityEvidence and AdoptKeyIdentity (iam-db#123), so the proof can run. (2) dial v0.2.25 to v0.2.26 (gateway, iam, iam-db, project, project-db, task, task-db): the range is one commit that bumps the yadgarhq/actions hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml; no source changes. (3) telemetry v0.2.0 to v0.2.7 (all seven): src changes only doc comments (D25 to D67); the rest is hook bumps and changes to telemetry's own Cargo.lock (tokio 1.53.2, the minor-and-patch group, pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 for RUSTSEC-2026-0414), which a consumer does not build from. (4) lifecycle v0.3.0 to v0.3.2 (iam, iam-db, project, project-db, task, task-db): two hook bumps; no source changes. lifecycle v0.2.17 to v0.3.2 (gateway): gateway uses the default rotate feature and not serve-tls, so the serve-tls changes (the ADR-1006 server limits of lifecycle#35, lifecycle#31, lifecycle#27, and the rustls and rustls-webpki RUSTSEC bumps, which are serve-tls dependencies) are not compiled into it. Two source changes reach gateway: drain_within now returns when the serving task ends on its own, so only a failure path such as a failed bind exits sooner (lifecycle#35); and rotate keeps every leaf of a Presented kind, with one CERTIFICATE_NOT_AFTER gauge per leaf, which leaves single-leaf callers unchanged (lifecycle#28). gateway's own Cargo.lock between 0.15.4 and 0.15.10 changes only the three yadgar crate sources, plus lifecycle's sha2 dependency edge 0.10.9 -> 0.11.1 (lifecycle#24, rotate's leaf fingerprint; sha2 0.11.1 was already in the lock, and the SHA-256 output is the same); no package is added or removed (301 at both tags). (5) store v0.6.0 to v0.6.4 (iam-db, project-db, task-db): migrate.rs changes only the LockUnavailable error text and doc comments (store#41), plus sha2 0.10.9 to 0.11.0 and hook bumps. The lock name stays yadgar_migrate:<database>; yadgar_migrate:iam, yadgar_migrate:project and yadgar_migrate:task are under the 64-character limit, so the SHA-256 path that sha2 feeds is not used, and no ledger DDL changes. iam-db v0.15.6 to v0.15.14, project-db v0.10.9 to v0.10.15 and task-db v0.11.10 to v0.11.17 add no migration (src/schema is untouched in each range). (6) platform 0.2.14 to 0.2.17: E1 rendered the five operator Applications at both versions with CRDs (158 objects: cert-manager 50, envoy-gateway 40, keda 29, mariadb-operator 32, prometheus 7) and found no changed object. The platform reason holds it only because the car C10 part 2 live-operator comparator is not built yet.

why: Max approved on 2026-11-07 a reviewed hand pin from 0.50.0 to 0.51.117 (auto-pin hold argocd#257). Each group was checked against a parent_render diff of both pins (83 objects, 13 hooks, hooks byte-identical) and the module and crate sources at their tags. (1) NATS, 6 reasons (ConfigMap nats-config, StatefulSet nats checksum, probes, hostAliases): platform 0.2.31 moves the monitor port 8222 from http_port to https_port (platform#76, ADR-0852). The client port 4222 tls block (verify true, no allow_non_tls) is unchanged, so no client changes and there is no ordering hazard. The startup and readiness probes become scheme HTTPS. The liveness wget calls https://nats:8222 with SSL_CERT_FILE set to the internal CA, and hostAliases maps nats to 127.0.0.1 so the nats-tls leaf (SAN nats) verifies. The changed checksum restarts the single NATS replica, and gateway and iam reconnect. No rendered object reads 8222 over http. (2) Env on iam, iam-db, project, project-db, task, task-db, 6 reasons: each adds LISTEN_MAX_CONNECTION_AGE_SECS=1800. No binary at these tags reads it: lifecycle v0.3.10 serve_tls/limits.rs defers the connection age to yaadgaar #417, and no module src reads the key. It is inert. (3) gateway env, 1 reason: YADGAR_ALLOWED_ORIGINS moves from empty to https://gateway.yadgar.internal (derived from global.hostname, gateway#185), and YADGAR_ALLOWED_ORIGINS_ALLOW_HTTP='0' is added. gateway 0.16 requires the switch at boot with no default (ADR-0569), and the value passes origin::check. Effect: a request whose Origin is https://gateway.yadgar.internal is now admitted; before, every browser Origin was refused. This is the DNS-rebinding check, not CORS. (4) Service and HTTPRoute gateway annotations, 2 reasons: argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options Prune=false (gateway#183). Argo never prunes the two objects; traffic does not change. (5) gateway E3 env readers, 10 reasons: src/origin.rs is the new allowlist reader of (3), and both of its keys render. src/boot/wiring.rs and the rest of src/boot/config.rs change only in comments; every key read there (TASK_, IAM_, PROJECT_ HOST, PORT and TLS keys, YADGAR_PROJECT_* keys) renders at both pins. (6) task E3, 2 reasons: src/main.rs changes only a comment (TASK_DB_TLS_ENABLED is required, ADR-0845). serve::from_env and UpstreamTls::from_env(TASK_DB) read TASK_DB_TLS_* and LISTEN_* keys that render at both pins. (7) seeder E3, 1 reason: seeder 0.3.17 dials iam on every run, so IAM_HOST, IAM_PORT, IAM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and IAM_TLS_CA_FILE are required; all four render in Job/seeder at both pins, and IAM_TLS_DOMAIN stays optional. (8) dial v0.2.26 to v0.2.32 (7 workloads): hook bumps, the licence, rust-version 1.99.1, tokio 1.54.1; no src change. dial v0.2.20 to v0.2.32 (seeder) adds the opt-in Deadline API (ADR-1019), a public CONNECT_TIMEOUT and the tokio and rustls-webpki RUSTSEC lock bumps. (9) lifecycle v0.3.2 to v0.3.10 (7 workloads): ServeTlsError::Unreadable no longer repeats its io reason (yaadgaar #290), plus rust 1.99.1, tests and hooks. lifecycle v0.2.23 to v0.3.10 (seeder) adds the ADR-1006 serve-tls limits and the drain that returns when the server ends; seeder serves nothing. (10) telemetry v0.2.7 to v0.2.15 (v0.2.16 for project-db, a dependency-group bump only): request_id::capped stores a request id over 256 characters cut, with '...' (task 371); pulldown-cmark 0.13.6 for RUSTSEC-2026-0433 is in telemetry's own lock. seeder moves from telemetry v0.2.0; v0.2.0 to v0.2.7 changes only doc comments (argocd#207). (11) store v0.6.4 to v0.8.2 (iam-db, project-db, task-db), E3 and E4: the first boot runs ALTER TABLE yadgar_schema_migrations ADD COLUMN checksum CHAR(64) NULL and backfills each row's checksum after a name check (store#52). Each boot then refuses a checksum mismatch, a ledger row the binary does not carry, or a hole below the newest row (store#74). The migration sets are unchanged in each range (iam-db 1-21, project-db 1-7, task-db 1-8; src/schema untouched), so no new DDL runs. store v0.6.4 names its ledger columns explicitly (SELECT MAX(version); INSERT (version, name)), so v0.50.0 binaries still boot on the altered ledger after a rollback. Before merge, Max reads each ledger and confirms it holds exactly these versions with these names.
